title: Who's Hiding from Eliezer?
summary: Eliezer gives away everything in his pocket, so the charity collectors hide from him! Behind barrels, among watermelons, even up a palm tree... but Eliezer always finds them. A funny, warm rhyming story about giving with a whole heart, based on the Talmud's tale of Eliezer of Bartota.
pages:
In a little village, among olives and figs,
lived Eliezer, who gave to the smalls and the bigs.
Whatever was in his pocket, he gave right away,
so the charity collectors... hid from him every day!

One day he went to market with a sack full of coins,
for his daughter's wedding: a dress and cakes to enjoy.
The collectors whispered, "Oh no, here he comes! Quick, behind the barrels, let's go!
If he finds us, he'll give us everything, and that just can't be so!"

But over the barrels two hats peeked out,
one tall and one round, both trembling about.
"One, two, three — I'm coming to seek!
Whoever is hiding gets something unique!"

They ran and jumped in a basket with twenty fat watermelons, round,
but two of the melons had a hat, a nose and a face that could be found!
"One, two, three — I'm coming to seek!
Whoever is hiding gets something unique!"

They climbed up a palm tree, high, high up to the skies,
but the palm tree suddenly grew... four legs, to everyone's surprise!
"One, two, three — I'm coming to seek!
Whoever is hiding gets something unique!"

The collectors climbed slowly down, with a palm leaf on each hat,
and Eliezer asked, "Who's the money for? Tell me! I want to hear all of that!"
"For a bride and a groom," they said, "who are orphans, both two —
they have no father or mother, and no money for a wedding canopy or flowers too."

Eliezer turned his sack upside down: "Take it! Take it all!
A wedding needs a canopy, and a cake as big as a great house, tall!"
Jingle, jingle! The coins rolled every which way,
and only one little coin was left in his pocket, among the crumbs where they lay.

And in the evening — a wedding! With a drum and a violin,
the bride and groom under the canopy, the whole village singing, all lit up within.
And the collectors? They danced and they hopped like two bunnies at play,
and Eliezer in the middle, happy, with everyone twirling his way.

With his very last coin he bought a tiny handful of wheat,
and poured it in a corner of the storehouse, small and neat.
In the evening Mom pulled the door — and the door wouldn't budge at all!
And from the crack — shhhhh! — wheat came pouring! The storehouse was full to the roof, like a tower tall!

And the next day, at market, among olives and figs,
over the barrels peeked... two little hats again, the smalls and the bigs!
"One, two, three — I'm coming to seek!
Whoever is hiding gets something unique!"
